question: In which year and city/cities India hosted the FIH Men’s World Cup?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2023 Bhubaneswar and Rourkela**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India hosted the FIH Men's World Cup in **2023**.
 
• The event was held in **Bhubaneswar and Rourkela**, cities located in the state of Odisha.
 
• The tournament took place from **January 13 to January 29, 2023**.
 
• This was the fourth time India hosted the FIH Men's World Cup, with previous editions in 1982, 2010, and 2018.
 
• The Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar and the newly constructed Birsa Munda International Hockey Stadium in Rourkela were the two venues for the matches.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **FIH Men's World Cup**

 
 
• Organized by the International Hockey Federation (FIH), the Men's Hockey World Cup is a prestigious field hockey competition.
 
• The tournament is held every four years, featuring the best national teams from around the world.
 
• The first edition of the Men's Hockey World Cup was held in 1971 in Barcelona, Spain.
 
• Pakistan has been the most successful team in the history of the tournament, winning it four times.
 
 
 
• **Kalinga Stadium**
 
 
• Located in Bhubaneswar, the Kalinga Stadium is a multi-purpose stadium primarily used for field hockey.
 
• It has hosted several international hockey tournaments, including the 2018 Men's Hockey World Cup.
 
• The stadium has a seating capacity of around 15,000 spectators.
 
 
 
• **Birsa Munda International Hockey Stadium**
 
 
• Situated in Rourkela, Odisha, this is a newly constructed stadium for the 2023 Men's Hockey World Cup.
 
• It is named after the tribal freedom fighter Birsa Munda.
 
• The stadium has a seating capacity of approximately 20,000, making it one of the largest hockey stadiums in India.
 
 
 
• **India's Hockey History**
 
 
• India has a rich history in field hockey, having won eight Olympic gold medals.
 
• The Indian men's hockey team is one of the most successful teams in the sport's history.
 
• India won the Hockey World Cup in 1975, held in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.
